value.origin: Common tangent-frame center; z=0 is arbitrary display depth, not the stellar plane.

evidence.limitations: Neither conditional compact-light depths nor display surface zero is a measured stellar/dust distance.

evidence.scope: All four complete registered rasters; 252 arcminute square processing frame
evidence.limitations: Different footprints and stretches. WISE outskirts lack optical/Spitzer coverage. RGB samples are relative appearance, not surface brightness.

evidence.scope: WISP UV and Burrell Schmidt B field
evidence.limitations: Difficult UV stellar PSF subtraction; intended polarimetry unsuccessful. No untouched UV raster, calibration arrays, masks or per-pixel uncertainties ingested.

value.ordering: West-side central dust is on average closer to stars than east-side dust; some second-layer dust may be among or behind stars.

evidence.limitations: Not measured voxel depths. Thin/plane-parallel geometry and multi-star illumination assumptions; outskirts 1-2 degrees away may have other illuminators. Single supported surface cannot represent both layers.

evidence.scope: Best-performing modified Gordon-Clayton-Witt model, UV only
evidence.limitations: Grain/bulk-medium interpretation and Henyey-Greenstein large-angle bias remain uncertain. These parameters are not applied to optical/IR RGB or the current positive-emission solver.

evidence.scope: Separate Schmidt, WIYN, HST, VLA and single-dish maps, each within stated frequency limits
evidence.limitations: Slope adopted visually; relative spectra rescaled; HI noise correction incomplete. Projected power is insensitive to morphology and cannot determine topology/depth. No fractal noise or inferred 3D spectrum synthesized.

evidence.scope: 2014 radio-bright member-star sample; historical distance measurement
evidence.limitations: Not the distance of each filament, illuminator or compact residual light. Not claimed as a current exhaustive Gaia-based cluster solution. No pc-to-depth conversion used in this baseline.

evidence.scope: 20 pencil beams, January 2002; Table 1 J2000 positions span RA 56.200917 to 57.718458 deg, Dec 23.147139 to 24.839250 deg
evidence.limitations: No continuous map or measured velocity-to-depth law. Ca II has several components; Doppler b is not centroid uncertainty. Original spectra and machine-readable per-component errors not imported, so no velocity fit is performed.

evidence.quantity: typical diffuse gas density from chemistry
evidence.scope: CH/CH+ and H2 rotational diagnostics on the measured sightlines
evidence.limitations: Conditional steady-state chemistry; time-dependent CH+ formation omitted. Dense HD23512 cloud is a distinct regime. This is not a calibrated dust density prior and is not assigned to every image pixel.
Anchor is a star direction, not a measured cloud center or footprint. Published reddening E(B-V)=0.35 mag and CH velocity +9.8 km/s concern this pencil beam only.
The archived stretched IRIS HiPS PNG is excluded from processing; its output sampling does not improve these beams. No SED, temperature or column density is fitted.

evidence.value: One smooth finite display-emission support; broad weak warp, central west/east tilt and local deformation around the HD23512 sightline.
evidence.scope: All covered images, with central literature guidance scoped locally
evidence.limitations: All amplitudes, thickness, radii and blend weights are authored. A local deformation does not recreate the second dust layer. No illumination, scattering, extinction, dust mass, hydrodynamics or independent stellar depth is solved.

evidence.unit: depth/radius/thickness arcsec; gradients dimensionless; curvature arcsec^-1
evidence.limitations: Display choices bounded before bake; not derived from image brightness, measured gas densities, 0.7 pc scattering model, or stellar distance.

limitations: Available one-surface positive-emission model only approximates display topology. Scattering and multiple overlapping layers remain unsupported.
No literature diagnostic is fitted quantitatively; reflection brightness is not dust density.
